Neutralize

/NOO-truh-lyz/ - the stress falls on NOO · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Neutralize means to cancel out the effect of something or make it harmless.

The negotiator neutralized the rival firm's biggest bargaining chip by publishing the disputed report herself.

Worked Example

The castle's designers neutralized the battering ram before one was ever built: the approach path turns twice, too tightly for any ram to swing.

Neutralize goes to the source: the threat itself is left harmless, unable to do what it was going to do. That is what separates it from merely opposing something — a neutralized venom, alarm, or argument isn't fought; it's switched off.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

defuse: To defuse is to take the tension out of a situation before it blows up — the danger drained is emotional: tempers, panics, crises of nerve. Neutralize aims at capability rather than mood: a neutralized threat — a venom, a weapon, an argument — still exists but can no longer do anything. You defuse feelings; you neutralize threats.

disarm: To disarm is to take the weapons, or the hostility, away from someone who holds them; a guard disarms an intruder, a warm answer disarms a critic. Neutralize is broader: it leaves any threat harmless at its source, whether or not anything is taken away. You disarm a holder; you neutralize the threat itself.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unleash: to release something at its full force

empower: to give something more ability to act

Where it sits · how much of the threat remains — weaken → neutralize → eliminate

weaken vs. neutralize: Weakening a threat is milder than neutralizing it — the danger is smaller, but it can still bite.

eliminate vs. neutralize: Eliminating goes even further than neutralizing — a neutralized threat still exists, just harmless, while an eliminated one is gone entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — neutr

Root — neutr: neither of two (Latin neuter, from ne + uter)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Suffix — -ize

Suffix — -ize: to make, to cause

Put it together

Put it together: Neutr (neither of two) + -al (relating to) + -ize (to make) = to make something belong to neither side. Latin neuter meant 'not either one'; to neutralize an acid, a threat, or an advantage is to push it to that no-man's-land where it works for nobody and harms nobody.

Use the root in a new word: neutron

Use the root in a new word: neutron: Physicists named the neutron for what it lacks: the particle carries neither a positive nor a negative charge.

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Neutralize is the word for switching a threat off at the source — chemists neutralize acids, defenders neutralize an attack, diplomats neutralize a crisis. Its unit-mate counteract fights an effect to a draw while the source keeps running; neutralize reaches the source and leaves it harmless. Use 'defuse' when what's being drained is tension rather than capability.
